findings.title: Iris Plaza EC Site Temporary Suspension Notice (first report) - Iris Ohyama
findings.summary_md: Iris Plaza, the Iris Ohyama group's official online store, published its first notice on October 29, 2026 after confirming unauthorized access to an external cloud service it used. The notice stated the EC site and related systems were suspended on October 28 when a suspicious file was found, and that the incident was reported to police and Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission the same day. At that point the possibility of personal information leakage was still under investigation.

findings.title: Unauthorized access to Iris Ohyama's e-commerce site; information leakage under investigation - ITmedia NEWS
findings.summary_md: ITmedia NEWS reported on October 30, 2026 that Iris Ohyama announced the previous day that its Iris Plaza online store had suffered unauthorized access and was temporarily suspended. The company said at that time that whether personal information had leaked was still under investigation. It also stated that credit card information leakage had not been confirmed.

findings.title: Iris Plaza: possible leak of personal information for about 7.7 million people, official second report - Security Measures Lab
findings.summary_md: Security Measures Lab published on October 30, 2026 that Iris Plaza found a suspicious file in an external cloud service on October 28, 2026 and immediately suspended the Iris Plaza EC site and related systems. The article records that unauthorized access was confirmed and reported to police and Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission on October 29. In its later update it reports the affected scope as about 7.7 million people, including about 5.8 million members and former members and about 1.9 million non-members, with credit card data not stored in the affected cloud service.

findings.title: Iris Plaza says cloud breach exposed data on 7.7 million customers
findings.summary_md: CyberInsider reported on November 5, 2026 that an external cloud service breach at Iris Plaza may have exposed personal data of about 7.7 million customers, including passwords. Credit card data was not stored in the affected cloud service and was not impacted. The company found suspicious files on October 28, shut down the store the same day, and reported the incident to police and Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission on October 29.

findings.title: Iris Ohyama: personal data of about 7.7 million customers may have leaked - Nikkei
findings.summary_md: Nikkei reported on November 5, 2026 that Iris Ohyama said about 7.7 million customer records stored for its Iris Plaza online store may have partially leaked after unauthorized access to an external cloud service. The affected data include names, addresses and phone numbers for about 5.8 million members including former members and about 1.9 million non-members, while credit card data was not included. The store was suspended on October 28 after a suspicious file was found and the company said it would contact potentially affected customers individually by email.

findings.title: Iris Ohyama official store Iris Plaza: possible leak of about 7.7 million people's personal information - ITmedia NEWS
findings.summary_md: ITmedia NEWS reported on November 6, 2026 that Iris Plaza announced on November 5 that about 7.7 million people's personal data stored in an external cloud service may have leaked. The breakdown is about 5.8 million members including former members and about 1.9 million non-members, with member fields such as name, address, phone, email, gender, encrypted password and date of birth, and non-member fields such as name, address, phone and email. Iris Plaza stated it would contact affected customers individually from November 5 and that no credit card data was stored in the affected cloud service.
